x: The entry of 137 was the largest of the season up to that time and the race resulted in a double scratch and handicap win, Syd Spencer gaining a well-deserved success in the individual handicap. In addition to this, Bob Readman was second in the handicap and F.
Also Mac's young brother Sid, and Fred Herring, now first claim, will soon be available for teams. To our new members we extend a very hearty welcome and wish them many happy years with the club.
Fred Herring, unfortunately, had to retire at 30 miles, but no doubt he will have another shot. In the R.W.A. 50 kilos at Eastleigh we again met with misfortune.
Although the majority of our opponents were Air Force Apprentices they showed great keenness and it looks at if Fred Herring is going to produce some real talent in a couple of years' time.

These included Charlie Churcher, who developed leg trouble, Pat Sapcote, Fred Herring, Jack Wakeley and Don Heath, so that by the end of the race we had just a bare four left, who finished in fourth position, 2 points behind Woodford.
Spencer and Fred Herring. Syd., walking in his first 100 miles, was quite happy all through the race and gave his faithful helpers not too hard a time.
In the same race Fred Herring, an R.A.F. man gained badge No. 191 in 21:50:00. We haven't seen Fred for a number of years but he did a lot to encourage Race Walking in the R.A.F. before retiring.
Gordon Doubleday, F.Herring, Sid Spencer and Bill Urry followed at an easier pace. Jack Bidgood eventually went away from the others and at Chequers Horley was in 9th position.
